Zatyshne Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zatyshne, Ukraine

Demolished. Jewish Colony Number 15 in Zatishye (now Zatyshne) was founded in 1853 by Jewish settlers from the Vitebsk and Mogilev Governorates in present-day Belarus. Population grew from 122 (1859) to 602 by 1877, despite a destructive 1885 fire; by 1897, 527 Jews (74%) supported a synagogue and a two-class school. A 1905 pogrom struck the colony, and Zionist activity followed the 1917 Revolution. During the 1918-21 Civil War, 13 Jews were killed and 30 houses burned in repeated pogroms. Soviet authorities established a Jewish collective farm in 1929, and Zatyshne became seat of a Jewish village council spanning Rivnopil and Khlibodarivka. Most residents evacuated before German forces arrived in October 1941, though some were captured while fleeing; in November 1941, 83 Jews from Zatyshne and Khlibodarivka were murdered. According to local testimony, the cemetery was later cleared for agricultural use, though the land itself was never plowed or cultivated - meaning the underlying burial sites likely remain intact despite the removed gravestones.
